3H.1 Flatter is not godly and is not to be used.
Understanding

precepts.text: There's a scripture that says days should speak, and multitude of years should show wisdom, but there's a spirit in man.
precepts.point: A brother: Which goes back to what you were saying. Remember, there's a scripture that says days should speak, and multitude of years should show wisdom, but there's a spirit in man. A lot of older brothers who lived from the time of the fifties and sixties, they amounted to nothing. But they want to be over men. But you have to study first. You have to learn God's laws and apply God's laws. But they feel because of their age they can be over younger men. No, you're not at that level yet. Spiritually, you're not growing. You're still at an infant stage. We don't care if you're eighty years old. If you don't know God's laws, you're an infant. You're a toddler according to the word of God. Everybody understand that?

note.label: From Milk to Meat: Train All Your Senses

precepts.why:
Sirach says “The law shall be found perfect without lies”, and “A man that hath travelled knoweth many things; and he that hath much experience will declare wisdom.” It is talking about the man that knows the law and travels. Some of you were in the military and traveled, and you don't know nothing. Some of you are old and traveled here and there, and you don't know nothing, only because you don't know the law. Travel and years do not make wisdom without God's laws.

That goes back to Job 32: days should speak, and the multitude of years should show wisdom, but there is a spirit in man. A lot of older brothers who lived from the time of the fifties and sixties amounted to nothing, but they want to be over men. You have to study first. You have to learn God's laws and apply God's laws. They feel because of their age they can be over younger men. No, you are not at that level yet. Spiritually you are not growing; you are still at an infant stage. We don't care if you are eighty years old: if you don't know God's laws, you are an infant, a toddler, according to the word of God.

The understanding does not come from the number of years but from the spirit God puts in a man. Military men who have been to Syria and Iraq don't know what they are looking at, because they are not studied to know what to look for. The man whose years and travels are joined to the law is the one that declares wisdom.

precepts.text: Let me not accept any man's person, neither let me give flattering titles unto man; for in so doing my maker would soon take me away. Accepting a man's person is partiality. We have noticed in some sanctuaries that brothers keep men around them because they are partial to them, while passing over the man with wisdom in the scriptures and skills, because the one that fits the bill is always correcting them. A brother with no skill set and very little wisdom made a high ranking officer is just a flattering title. Job said God will kill you for that, because you put friendship over what the scriptures say. You want men around you that will tell you when you are wrong; if everything you say is right, you are setting yourself up for a fall. If you are the smartest one in the room, you better find another room.
precepts.point: All the men in the scriptures that set order and structure were disliked: Jeremiah, Ezekiel, the apostles, Paul, Samuel, Christ. If you are a man about structure, order, and discipline in your household, you are going to be the least liked. But if you are a man of the truth, you do not care; your job is to structure and order. Men, your job is to raise up the 144,000.
precepts.why:
“Let me not, I pray you, accept any man's person, neither let me give flattering titles unto man.” Accepting a man's person is partiality. In some IUIC sanctuaries, brothers keep men around them because they are partial to them and like them. That is not scriptural. A man with wisdom in the scriptures, with skills, who knows how to deal with the people, gets passed over for the guy who kisses your behind.

A brother with no skill set and very little wisdom, made a captain or a high ranking officer: that's just a flattering title. He don't fit the bill. Officers of fifty, sixty, ten and twenty were asked to paraphrase Genesis on Abraham, father of many nations, and none of them could break it down. How did they get these titles?

“For I know not to give flattering titles; in so doing my maker would soon take me away.” God will kill you for that, because you put friendship over what the scriptures say: I like this friend better than the one that fits the bill, because the one that fits the bill is always correcting me. You want men like that around you. No dummies, no yes-men. If I say or do something wrong, I expect the men around me to say, Bishop, don't say that, don't do that.

When everything you say is right, you're a fool, setting yourself up for a fall. If you're the smartest one in the room, you better get out of the room and surround yourself with brothers that got some sense. That is order: men placed by what the scriptures say, not by flattery.

precepts.text: I know not to give flattering titles; in so doing my Maker would soon take me away. Ask for the title, get the test, fail the test. When the student is ready the teacher appears; promotion comes from the Lord once you fulfil the office you are in.
precepts.point: Are you ready to be examined as an example when you leave the school, with your wife, with your children, in what you eat, in how you treat your temple? All of that is leadership.

note.label: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

precepts.why:
“For I know not to give flattering titles; in so doing my maker would soon take me away.” When you get the flattering title, your maker soon takes you away. What does that mean? You want the flattering title, you get the test, you fail the test. Bam. Thought I was worthy. Nope.

So be mindful of what you ask for. Brothers work underhandedly to become leaders, and it don't work like that; this is the Lord's business, and he is the one giving it out. Brothers that ask for rank, that say give me the 50's test, never make it, and that is how you know Satan is pushing them. When brothers ask for the test, nine times out of ten they fail it, because spiritually you are not ready if you are asking. Nobody asks to be a leader. The Lord raised all these men up. The Bishop didn't ask to be a bishop; he became a bishop. If you are asking for it, you are in the wrong place.

When the student is ready, the teacher will be there. The Lord will place you where you are supposed to be; promotion comes from the Lord, and there is a reason you are in the position you are in. Once you fulfill that office, the Lord will make it happen. Many brothers who wanted position fell down and never made it back, while others who were down came back on fire. The work determines where you are supposed to be. Brothers get jealous when another brother gets position, but if you love the Lord you work for the Lord, not for position. In Maccabees the brother who said let me get me a name ended up put to death.

That is what Judith 8:24 asks of a leader: not a title, but “let us shew an example to our brethren, because their hearts depend upon us”. The higher up you go, the more people you serve. If you don't have the mindset to build up those beneath you and to support and push up the leader above you, forget it; the Lord can't use you.

precepts.text: Now mine eye seeth thee, wherefore I abhor myself and repent in dust and ashes. Job repented for justifying himself instead of the Lord.
precepts.point: The three men ceased to answer Job because he was righteous in his own eyes, and Elihu's wrath was kindled because Job justified himself rather than God. Job said he was not weak like Adam. That was his flaw: he was over-righteous.
precepts.why:
Job ends where chapter 32 began. There the three men ceased to answer him “because he was righteous in his own eyes”, and Elihu was angry “because he justified himself rather than God.” Here Job says, “I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear: but now mine eye seeth thee. Wherefore I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes.”

Job hated himself and repented. He repented for justifying himself and not God, for being righteous in his own eyes. He had said, I am righteous, this is not supposed to happen to me; I made a covenant with mine eyes, I don't look at other women, I am not weak like Adam, I don't hide sin in my bosom. That was his flaw. He was over-righteous, and the Lord did not like it.

In his own eyes Job did not look at it as though there was a reason God was doing this, that God was trying to make him better. In his mind it was, I am righteous, I am not like this person or that person. So the Bible says, “Be not righteous over much; neither make thyself over wise: why shouldest thou destroy thyself?” That person who tries to act over-righteous just ends up looking fake; nobody knows everything and nobody is perfect.

This is the war within, the war nobody sees. Everything Job suffered before was physical, but Satan was attacking his mind too. The Lord used what Job went through to show him what was inside himself, and that is what Satan's attacks do: they show you things inside yourself. Through all of it Job was made perfect, and he came out of it repenting in dust and ashes, justifying God instead of himself.

precepts.text: Days should speak and multitude of years should teach wisdom, but great men are not always wise, neither do the aged understand judgment; the multitude of years should have taught our people wisdom about the judgments, but they do not have it.
precepts.point: The fear of the Lord is clean, enduring for ever; the judgments of the Lord are true and righteous altogether. This whole Bible is the ways of the Lord, the judgments of the Lord, true and righteous altogether; if you want to know what righteousness is you have to learn and follow the Bible.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
“I said, Days should speak, and multitude of years should teach wisdom.” The multitude of years should have taught our people wisdom about the judgments of the Lord, but they do not have it.

“But there is a spirit in man: and the inspiration of the Almighty giveth them understanding. Great men are not always wise: neither do the aged understand judgment.” Understanding comes from the inspiration of the Almighty, not from age; great men are not always wise, and the aged do not understand judgment.

The judgments of the Lord are true and righteous altogether, and to know them you have to learn and follow the Bible, not lean on years.

precepts.text: Days should speak and multitude of years should teach wisdom, but it is the spirit and the inspiration of the Almighty, keeping and applying the laws of the Most High, that gives understanding; great men are not always wise.
precepts.point: I have refrained my feet from every evil way, that I might keep Thy word. I have not departed from Thy judgments, for Thou hast taught me. How sweet are Thy words unto my taste, sweeter than honey to my mouth. Through Thy precepts I get understanding, therefore I hate every false way.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“I have more understanding than all my teachers: for thy testimonies are my meditation. I understand more than the ancients, because I keep thy precepts.” Job says how that can be: “I said, Days should speak, and multitude of years should teach wisdom. But there is a spirit in man: and the inspiration of the Almighty giveth them understanding.”

You would expect the aged to have the wisdom, but it is the spirit and the inspiration of the Almighty, keeping and applying the laws of the Most High, that gives understanding. “Great men are not always wise: neither do the aged understand judgment.”

So through his commandments a man is made wiser than his enemies and understands more than the ancients. The law has to be our meditation all the day; through his precepts we get understanding, and therefore we hate every false way.

points: But there is a spirit in man: and the inspiration of the Almighty giveth them understanding. So there is a spirit in man, and that spirit begins from the time of the womb. There is a spirit in man, there is a spirit in woman. And the inspiration of the Almighty gives them the understanding.

So the spirit is placed on us from the time of the womb. We just do not know it yet. We thought when we were born we were to be a mama's boy, or to be in Pee Wee leagues, or in Pop Warner, or whatever. We all have our way of thinking our life is supposed to turn out. But that is not necessarily what God had ordained since the time you were in your mother's womb.

The three men ceased to answer Job because he was righteous in his own eyes, and Elihu's wrath was kindled because Job justified himself rather than God. Job said he was not weak like Adam. That was his flaw: he was over-righteous.

These three men ceased to answer Job because he was righteous in his own eyes. Then the wrath of Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the kindred of Ram, was kindled against Job because he justified himself rather than God.

Elihu recognized who his elders were. He did not talk out of turn or try to make himself equal to them. He sat back like a young man should, let the older men discuss what they needed to discuss, and came afterward once they were finished.

note.label: Job 32: The Wrath Of Elihu The Young Man

points: Elihu's wrath was also kindled against the three friends because they found no answer and yet condemned Job. Elihu had waited until Job had spoken because they were elder than he. This is a young man, and in this chapter alone you learn a lot about how young men should be with men that are aged, especially wise men in this truth.

note.label: Job 32: The Wrath Of Elihu The Young Man

points: Elihu answered and said he is young and they are very old, so he was afraid and durst not show his opinion. He said days should speak and multitude of years should teach wisdom.

note.label: Job 32: The Wrath Of Elihu The Young Man

points: But there is a spirit in man, and the inspiration of the Almighty giveth them understanding. Great men are not always wise, neither do the aged always understand judgment; therefore he says hearken unto me, I also will show mine opinion.

note.label: Job 32: The Wrath Of Elihu The Young Man

points: Elihu waited for their words and gave ear to their reasons while they searched out what to say. He attended unto them and behold there was none that convinced Job or answered his words.

note.label: Job 32: The Wrath Of Elihu The Young Man

points: Lest they should say they have found out wisdom, he warns that God thrusteth Job down, not man. Now Job has not directed his words against Elihu, neither will Elihu answer him with their speeches. Once Elihu saw that Job justified himself and the other men had nothing else to say, he had to say something.

note.label: Job 32: The Wrath Of Elihu The Young Man

points: They were amazed and answered no more; they left off speaking. When Elihu had waited and they stood still and answered no more, he said he too will show his opinion, for he is full of matter and the spirit within him constraineth him.

note.label: Job 32: The Wrath Of Elihu The Young Man

points: His belly is as wine which hath no vent, ready to burst like new bottles. He will speak that he may be refreshed. He will not accept any man's person nor give flattering titles, for he knows not to give flattering titles, and in so doing his Maker would soon take him away. This is the four chapters in Job for today.

note.label: Job 32: The Wrath Of Elihu The Young Man
